author: Ryan
experience: Stayed here about 5 times, plus many visits to eat
take:
I've stayed at the Yacht Club about five times, and I've been back many more times just to eat. Most recently I was there a few weeks ago for lunch at Ale & Compass. When you walk in, it really feels like stepping into a true yacht club, and there's a distinctive smell in the lobby that always makes me feel at home.

What I love most is being on the BoardWalk. Step outside and the whole area is right there, whether you're walking over to Epcot or taking a late-night stroll. All three BoardWalk-area resorts have that feel, and it's one of my favorite spots on property. The price to get in is high, but I think it's worth the extra money.
suits: Couples and families who want to walk to Epcot, love a great pool, and want a polished, relaxing Deluxe stay on the BoardWalk.
rooms:
The rooms are nice, a little darker than at some other resorts, but the recent refresh gives them a new, modern touch of luxury. It really stood out compared to my previous stay.

Any water or pool view is always great, but those come at a premium. If you want to save a little, a garden view is totally fine, especially since the price to stay here is already high.

Standard rooms sleep up to five, and Club Level rooms add access to a concierge lounge.
pools:
Stormalong Bay is my favorite thing about this resort. It still has the sand at the bottom, which is so unique, and it always made me excited to jump in whenever I stayed at the Yacht or Beach Club. It's a huge pool area shared with the Beach Club, with a lazy river, a shipwreck slide, hot tubs and a kids' area. Only Yacht and Beach Club guests can use it.

If you want something calmer, the Yacht Club also has a quieter leisure pool away from the crowds.
dining:
My favorite place to eat here is Ale & Compass. I love the buffalo cauliflower bites.

Yachtsman Steakhouse is extremely good. My wife and I have eaten there quite a few times and have never had a bad steak. It's always been a great experience. It reopened in 2026 after a refresh. Crew's Cup Lounge, next door, is very good too, and you don't need a reservation.

For quick service, The Market at Ale & Compass is near the lobby gift shop. Get the chocolate chip muffins: they're so good, and a great breakfast whenever I stay here.

Also nearby: Hurricane Hanna's by the pool, and at the Beach Club next door, Beaches & Cream and Cape May Cafe.
gettingAround:
I usually walk into Epcot through the International Gateway and take the Skyliner to Hollywood Studios. For the other parks, I drive.

  • The walk to Epcot's International Gateway takes about 5 to 10 minutes.
  • There's no Skyliner station at the resort itself. The closest one is at the International Gateway, a short walk away.
  • Friendship boats also run to Hollywood Studios, and it's a nice walk along the water if you'd rather stroll.
  • Buses to Magic Kingdom and Animal Kingdom share stops with other resorts and can be slow, so leave extra time if you're not driving.
pros: Stormalong Bay, with its sand-bottom pool
Walking to Epcot and the whole BoardWalk area
Refreshed rooms with a modern touch of luxury
cons: It's one of the priciest Deluxe resorts, and water views cost extra.
Buses to Magic Kingdom and Animal Kingdom can be slow.
The rooms run a little darker than at some other resorts.
Exterior work at the Beach Club next door is scheduled to continue into late 2027, so check what's affected before your trip.
tips: Save room in your budget by booking a garden view. You'll still be steps from the pool and the BoardWalk.
Grab a chocolate chip muffin at The Market at Ale & Compass for an easy breakfast.
Take an evening stroll on the BoardWalk after dinner.
Get to Stormalong Bay early in the day or late in the afternoon for the best spot.
The Skyliner closes for refurbishment January 24 to 30, 2027, with buses filling in. Plan Hollywood Studios days around that if you're traveling then.
bestFor: Couples and families who want to walk to Epcot and spend time at the best pool on property.
